Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/spi/spi.c`**
1. **Line Addition**: A new line `ret = -ENOMSG;` is added at the beginning of the `__spi_map_msg` function to initialize the return value.
2. **Conditional Check**: A new conditional check is added to return `0` (success) if no transfers have been mapped, indicated by the `if (ret)` condition.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in `spi.c` are aimed at improving the handling of SPI messages that do not contain any mapped transfers. By initializing the return value to `-ENOMSG` and checking this value before proceeding, the function can now exit early with a success status if there are no transfers to map. This change prevents the unnecessary setting of the DMA mapped flag and avoids potential issues with DMA-related APIs being called on unmapped data. The patch addresses a specific bug introduced in a previous commit, ensuring that the code behaves correctly when handling empty SPI messages.

Reason:
The bug occurs because the code incorrectly sets `ctlr->cur_msg_mapped` to `true` even when there are no valid transfers in the SPI message. The loop iterates over the transfers, but if none are mapped (i.e., if `can_dma` returns false for all transfers), the message is still marked as DMA mapped, leading to potential misuse of DMA-related APIs on unmapped data.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
ret = -ENOMSG;
```
```c
if (ret)
    return 0;
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a check for the `ret` variable, which is set to `-ENOMSG` if no transfers are mapped. If `ret` remains non-zero after the loop, the function returns early, preventing the message from being marked as DMA mapped when there are no valid transfers. This ensures that the code does not proceed to use DMA APIs on unmapped data, thus avoiding undefined behavior.

content: You are a programming expert.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the incorrect handling of SPI messages that do not contain any mapped transfers. The code was erroneously marking the message as DMA mapped even when there were no transfers, which could lead to the invocation of DMA-related APIs on unmapped data, potentially causing undefined behavior or crashes.
        
        Commit message:
        spi: Don't mark message DMA mapped when no transfer in it is

There is no need to set the DMA mapped flag of the message if it has
no mapped transfers. Moreover, it may give the code a chance to take
the wrong paths, i.e. to exercise DMA related APIs on unmapped data.
Make __spi_map_msg() to bail earlier on the above mentioned cases.

Fixes: 99adef310f68 ("spi: Provide core support for DMA mapping transfers")
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://msgid.link/r/20240522171018.3362521-2-andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/spi/spi.c b/drivers/spi/spi.c
index a8966caed841..d40ce0fdb1a8 100644
--- a/drivers/spi/spi.c
+++ b/drivers/spi/spi.c
@@ -1243,6 +1243,7 @@ static int __spi_map_msg(struct spi_controller *ctlr, struct spi_message *msg)
 	else
 		rx_dev = ctlr->dev.parent;
 
+	ret = -ENOMSG;
 	list_for_each_entry(xfer, &msg->transfers, transfer_list) {
 		/* The sync is done before each transfer. */
 		unsigned long attrs = DMA_ATTR_SKIP_CPU_SYNC;
@@ -1272,6 +1273,9 @@ static int __spi_map_msg(struct spi_controller *ctlr, struct spi_message *msg)
 			}
 		}
 	}
+	/* No transfer has been mapped, bail out with success */
+	if (ret)
+		return 0;
 
 	ctlr->cur_rx_dma_dev = rx_dev;
 	ctlr->cur_tx_dma_dev = tx_dev;
--
